lessons.title: Practical Reference
lessons.body:
Practical Reference: Travel and Accommodation in Mandarin for African Agribusiness Professionals

For African agribusiness professionals travelling to China for trade fairs, supplier audits, cold-chain equipment inspections or farm-technology summits, the ability to handle hotels, transport and destinations in Mandarin is not a cultural nicety â it is a commercial advantage. A buyer who can confirm a late check-out before a factory visit, rebook a high-speed train after a delayed flight, or negotiate an airport transfer in Chinese saves hours and avoids costly misunderstandings. This reference consolidates the language and logistics you need across the module Travel and Accommodation, covering the lessons Booking a Hotel Room, Checking In and Out, Asking About Hotel Amenities, Travel Destinations and Attractions, Buying Train and Plane Tickets, and Role-Play: At the Hotel Front Desk.

1. Booking a Hotel Room (é¢è®¢éåº)

Book before you fly, and book in Chinese where possible. Platforms such as Ctrip (æºç¨) and Meituan (ç¾å¢) list business hotels near exhibition centres like the Canton Fair Complex in Guangzhou or the National Exhibition and Convention Center in Shanghai. Foreign travellers in China must register their accommodation with local police within 24 hours of arrival. Hotels do this automatically; if you stay in a private residence, you must register at the local police station (æ´¾åºæ) yourself. Carry your passport at all times â it is required for hotel check-in, train boarding and police checks. Never overstay your visa: penalties include fines of up to RMB 10,000, detention and future entry bans. For payments, WeChat Pay and Alipay now accept international cards, but carry some cash (RMB) for small vendors and taxis. Keep digital and paper copies of your passport, visa and hotel bookings in case of loss.

Quick Reference Checklist

  • Book hotel and high-speed rail tickets before departure; passport number must match exactly.
  • Save your hotel address in Chinese characters to show taxi drivers.
  • Confirm check-out time (usually 12:00) and request late check-out in advance.

  • Check halal or vegetarian dining options near your hotel if required.
  • Keep a printed backup of bookings, visa and emergency contacts (your embassy in China).
